title: Regulatory Networks of Upland and Lowland Ecotypes of Switchgrass Under Drought and Salt Stresses
author: Chunman Zuo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.saxeafn
materials: Dynamic regulatory maps DREM 2.0.3 # run software 'drem.jar' file in the directory of DREM software installation directory. The method of DREM takes as input fold-change (treated relative to untreated) time series data and transcription factor-gene interaction data, and produces as output a dynamic regulatory map. Windows - Jave

steps.title: Download raw RNA‑seq reads
steps.instruction: Use the NCBI SRA Toolkit (v2.8.2‑1) fastq‑dump to download each Illumina HiSeq 2500 RNA‑seq sample listed in the BioProject (accession PRJN). For every SRR code, run fastq‑dump with the options “‑I --split‑files” and direct the output to the fastq output directory ($out_dir).

steps.title: Trim adapters and filter reads
steps.instruction: Run BBDuk (v35.82) on each pair of fastq files to (i) trim adapters and low‑quality bases, and (ii) remove phiX174 contaminant reads.

substeps.instruction: system("$bbduk -Xmx5g in=$fq_file_1 in2=$fq_file_2 out=$fq_file_trim_1 out2=$fq_file_trim_2 ref=$adapter_seq threads=10 qtrim=rl trimq=10 ktrim=r k=23 mink=11 hdist=1 tpe tbo");

system("$bbduk -Xmx5g in=$fq_file_trim_1 in2=$fq_file_trim_2 out=$fq_file_final_1 out2=$fq_file_final_2 outm=$fq_file_m_1 outm2=$fq_file_m_2 ref=$contam_seq threads=10 k=31 hdist=1 stats=$fq_match_status");

steps.title: Build HISAT2 index
steps.instruction: Create a HISAT2 (v2.1.0) index for the switchgrass reference genome fasta ($genome_fa) in a new subdirectory called “index”.

steps.title: Map reads to genome
steps.instruction: Align each trimmed, contaminant‑free read pair to the switchgrass genome using HISAT2 with one best alignment per read.

steps.title: Normalize and test differential expression
steps.instruction: Use edgeR (v3.20.9) in R to filter low‑count genes, normalize counts by the TMM method, and identify genes that are significantly up‑ or down‑regulated between treatment (group A) and control (group B).

substeps.instruction: keep <- rowSums(reads_count >= 1) >= ceiling(0.9 * length(sample_group))   # filter low counts
Identify column indices for treated (A) and untreated (B) samples (e.g., treat_loc1, untreat_loc1).
d_s <- DGEList(counts = temp_data, group = c(rep("A", length(treat_loc1)), rep("B", length(untreat_loc1))))
lrt <- glmLRT(fit, coef = 2)   # compare A vs B

steps.title: Build co‑expression network
steps.instruction: For each stress condition, compute Pearson correlation between every differentially expressed transcription factor (TF) and target gene (TG); retain TF‑TG pairs with |PCC| > 0.70 and p‑value < 0.05 as putative regulatory edges.

substeps.instruction: TFs_diff <- vector of DE TF identifiers
TGs_diff <- vector of DE TG identifiers
TF_TG_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(TFs_diff), ncol = length(TGs_diff))

steps.title: Infer TF activity with NCA
steps.instruction: Run the NCA toolbox (version 2.3) in MATLAB to decompose the expression matrix and the TF‑TG adjacency matrix into transcription‑factor activities and control‑strength matrices.

substeps.instruction: – TF‑TG regulatory relationship matrix (from previous step).
The toolbox returns TF activity scores and control‑strength values.

steps.title: Perform GO enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Use topGO (v2.30.1) in R to test for enrichment of Biological Process (BP), Molecular Function (MF) and Cellular Component (CC) GO terms among a set of interest genes (inter_genes) against the full switchgrass annotation.

substeps.instruction: GOdata_BP <- new("topGOdata", ontology = "BP", allGenes = geneList, annot = annFUN.gene2GO, gene2GO = geneID2GO)
allRes_BP <- GenTable(GOdata_BP, classic = BP_fisher, orderBy = "weight", ranksOf = "classic", topNodes = length(which(BP_fisher@score < 0.01)))
write.table(allRes_BP, file = paste0(save_path_, codition, "_BP.txt"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
GOdata_MF <- new("topGOdata", ontology = "MF", allGenes = geneList, annot = annFUN.gene2GO, gene2GO = geneID2GO)
allRes_MF <- GenTable(GOdata_MF, classic = MF_fisher, orderBy = "weight", ranksOf = "classic", topNodes = length(which(MF_fisher@score < 0.01)))
write.table(allRes_MF, file = paste0(save_path_, codition, "_MF.txt"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
GOdata_CC <- new("topGOdata", ontology = "CC", allGenes = geneList, annot = annFUN.gene2GO, gene2GO = geneID2GO)
allRes_CC <- GenTable(GOdata_CC, classic = CC_fisher, orderBy = "weight", ranksOf = "classic", topNodes = length(which(CC_fisher@score < 0.01)))
write.table(allRes_CC, file = paste0(save_path_, codition, "_CC.txt"), sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
